remediation.fix_approach: Replaced document.write() string concatenation with safe DOM construction using createElement() + textContent assignment in formatPrintPage(). Content is now rendered as plain text, not parsed as HTML.
remediation.root_cause:
formatPrintPage() in AppComponent called popupWindow.document.write('
' + element + '
') where element is server-supplied ApplinX terminal field content. No HTML encoding was applied, allowing injection of script tags or event handlers that would execute in the same-origin print popup and could steal gx_token from sessionStorage.
changes_made: src/app/app.component.ts formatPrintPage(): replaced document.write() with createElement('div') + div.textContent = element. Browser never parses content as HTML.
remediation.verification_needed: Manual: trigger Print with a screen containing HTML content like ''. The popup should display the literal text, not execute the script. Confirm normal text content renders correctly.
remediation.defense_in_depth: textContent assignment is the safe API — no encoding step needed because the browser never interprets the assigned string as markup. Additional: consider adding Content-Security-Policy header at the web server level.
remediation.testing: Test print functionality with normal ASCII text, special characters (<>&"), and an XSS payload. All should render as visible text in the popup.
remediation.residual_risk: Low. Server-controlled field content now reaches only textContent — no HTML injection path. The copy modal was confirmed as a false positive (innerText path already safe).
